mainTopic: Setting aside the כתובה and selling the rest, and whether a sale the רבנן forbade still takes effect (רב יוסף versus אביי)
overview: The גמרא asks why a יבם can't just set aside the amount of the כתובה and sell the rest of the property. It answers that the משנה's line about not putting the כתובה "on the table" is only עצה טובה (good advice), and proves this from the סיפא about an ordinary husband. רבי אבא's harder method is explained as a way to avoid איבה between husband and wife. Then comes a story from פומבדיתא: a יבם promised his brother half the property so the brother would not disqualify the יבמה with a גט. רב יוסף rules that the promise means nothing, because a sale the רבנן said not to make does not take effect. אביי disagrees, citing a משנה where a forbidden sale still stands. The question is sent to two scholars, and רב מניומי rules like אביי. רב יוסף then brings a ברייתא about a debt owed to the dead brother, but רב נחמן says this ברייתא is not reliable. His reason is that the debtor can tell the יבמה, "You are not my litigant."

steps.title: Why not set aside only the כתובה amount and sell the rest?
steps.stepSummary: If a כתובה can be collected during the husband's lifetime, the יבם should be able to set aside just the כתובה amount for her and sell the rest of the property.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we think a כתובה can be collected while the husband is alive, then let him set aside for her property worth the amount of the כתובה, and sell the rest!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that a כתובה can be collected while the husband is alive. If that were true, there would be an easy fix: set aside the כתובה amount and sell the rest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumes that if her claim can be paid out during his lifetime, then her claim covers only a fixed amount. If so, nothing should tie up all of his property. So the earlier requirement that seems to lock up everything looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: It enters our mind (we would have thought)
A כתובה can be collected during the husband's lifetime

phrases.english: And if it enters our mind
that a כתובה can be collected during his lifetime,
let him set aside for her the amount of the כתובה,
and the rest let him sell!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of whether a כתובה can be collected during the husband's lifetime.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a כתובה can be collected during the husband's lifetime.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the claim can be paid out now, then only the כתובה amount needs to be held back, so the rest of the property should be free to sell.

steps.title: Counter-question: our משנה says the same thing
steps.stepSummary: The answerer replies that, by that reasoning, the questioner should have asked from our משנה itself, which says he may not put the כתובה "on the table" for her, and that all his property is mortgaged to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your logic, ask it from our משנה! It says he may not tell her, "Your כתובה is placed for you on the table." Rather, all his property is mortgaged to her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of answering directly, the גמרא throws the question back: the same problem shows up in our משנה. This sets up the real answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to forbid setting aside a fixed amount for the כתובה. So if this is a problem, it is a problem for the משנה too, not just for the earlier source. By widening the question, the answerer prepares one answer that will cover both.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning (a counter-question)
Placed on the table (set aside separately)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new attack on the opinion. It is a way of saying: "Your question applies to the משנה too, and the answer there will be the answer here."

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, let him raise it from our משנה:
He may not say to her,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי כְּתוּבָּתִיךְ מוּנַּחַת לִיךְ עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן,
phrases.english: "Here, your כתובה is placed for you on the table,"
phrases.notes: This means: here is your כתובה money set aside, so the rest of my property is free.

phrases.english: rather, all his property is mortgaged to her כתובה?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counters step 1 by showing the same difficulty exists in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The questioner's choice of source, and the משנה itself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה also seems to forbid setting aside only the כתובה amount, so the question should be asked there.

steps.title: The משנה is only giving good advice
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's instruction not to set aside the כתובה "on the table" is good advice, not a strict prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is teaching us good advice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is only giving practical advice. It is not saying it is forbidden to set aside the כתובה amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Setting aside one fixed pile for the כתובה is risky, because if that pile is lost her protection is gone. So the משנה advises keeping all the property as her guarantee. That is wise advice, but it is not a law against selling.

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם עֵצָה טוֹבָה קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.
phrases.english: There, it teaches us good advice.
phrases.notes: "There" means our משנה, which was just quoted.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם עֵצָה טוֹבָה קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty raised from the משנה in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the משנה as advice rather than law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה forbids setting aside only the כתובה amount.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה only advises against it; it is allowed by law.

steps.title: Proof from the סיפא about an ordinary husband
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא says the same line about an ordinary husband, who certainly may sell his property, so there too it must be advice. That means the רישא about the יבם is also advice.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you don't say so, look at the סיפא: "And similarly a man may not say to his wife, 'Your כתובה is placed for you on the table'; rather all his property is mortgaged to his wife's כתובה." If he wants to sell, can he really not sell here too?! Rather, it teaches good advice. So here too, it teaches good advice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the "good advice" reading from the second half of the same משנה, which is about an ordinary husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees an ordinary husband may sell his property. Yet the סיפא uses the same wording for him, so the wording must be advice there. Since the wording is the same, the first clause about the יבם is also just advice.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you do not say so
The latter clause of the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: The line "don't put her כתובה on the table" is good advice to protect her, not a ban on selling property.

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
the latter clause, which teaches:
"And similarly, a man may not say to his wife,
'Here, your כתובה is placed for you on the table';

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כׇּל נְכָסָיו אַחְרָאִין לִכְתוּבַּת אִשְׁתּוֹ —
phrases.english: rather, all his property is mortgaged to his wife's כתובה" —
if he wants to sell,
here too, is it that he cannot sell?!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עֵצָה טוֹבָה קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן,
phrases.english: Rather, it teaches us good advice,

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי עֵצָה טוֹבָה קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן,
phrases.english: so here too, it teaches us good advice.
phrases.notes: "Here" means the first clause, about the יבם.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 3 with proof from the סיפא.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה's wording is good advice, not law.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה, about an ordinary husband who clearly may sell.

steps.title: Then רבי אבא's ruling is a problem again
steps.stepSummary: If one may set aside the כתובה amount and sell the rest, then רבי אבא's earlier ruling, which requires a bigger step, seems unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, is רבי אבא's teaching difficult?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that setting aside the כתובה amount is allowed, the גמרא asks why רבי אבא required a more drastic step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא taught that a husband who wants to sell must take a harder route (divorcing her and taking her back). If simply setting aside the כתובה amount works, that harder route looks unnecessary, so his ruling is questioned again.

phrases.english: But then, is the teaching of רבי אבא difficult?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion of step 4 to reopen a question on רבי אבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא's ruling that a husband who wants to sell must take the harder route.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If setting aside the כתובה amount is allowed, there is no need for the harder method.

steps.title: רבי אבא's reason: avoiding bad feelings
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא's ruling is not a problem, because the reason is איבה. Setting aside her כתובה would make her feel he wants to be rid of her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא's teaching is also not difficult, because of enmity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אבא's ruling is about keeping peace between husband and wife, not about what the law allows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Setting aside her כתובה money could make the wife feel he is preparing to get rid of her, and that causes איבה. The harder route avoids that feeling, which is why רבי אבא chose it. So his ruling stands even though setting aside the amount is technically allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: Setting aside the כתובה amount is allowed by law. רבי אבא's harder method is only there to prevent איבה between husband and wife.

phrases.english: The teaching of רבי אבא is also not difficult,
because of enmity.
phrases.notes: He means she would feel hurt, as if he were getting ready to send her away.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא, מִשּׁוּם אֵיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty on רבי אבא from step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the ruling (relationship concern, not legal necessity).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אבא required the harder method because setting aside the כתובה amount is not allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Setting aside is allowed; רבי אבא's method is to avoid איבה.

steps.title: A new story: a יבמה in פומבדיתא
steps.stepSummary: A man had a יבמה come before him in פומבדיתא, and his brother wanted to disqualify her from him by giving her a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man had a יבמה come before him for יבום in פומבדיתא. His brother wanted to disqualify her from him with a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new real-life case. This sets up a question that will be discussed next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When one of the brothers gives the יבמה a גט, she can no longer do יבום with the other brothers. Here one brother wants to use that rule to keep her from marrying his brother. Steps 8 and 9 tell how the case turns out.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow who is waiting for יבום with her late husband's brother

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דִּנְפַלָה לֵיהּ יְבָמָה בְּפוּמְבְּדִיתָא,
phrases.english: A certain man had a יבמה come before him in פומבדיתא,
phrases.notes: Literally "fell to him": his brother died without children, so she became bound to him for יבום.

phrases.english: his brother wanted to disqualify her
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't; it just repeats "her".

phrases.english: from him by means of a גט.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דִּנְפַלָה לֵיהּ יְבָמָה בְּפוּמְבְּדִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new case story after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets out the case: a brother wants to disqualify the יבמה from his brother by giving her a גט.

steps.title: The יבם offers to split the property
steps.stepSummary: The brother who wants to do יבום asks the other brother why he wants to block him with a גט, and offers to share the property.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What are you thinking? Is this about the property? I will split the property with you.
steps.whatsHappening: The story from step 7 continues. The brother who wants to marry the יבמה guesses the other brother is worried about losing the inheritance, so he promises to share it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the brother who does יבום gets the dead brother's property. If the other brother gives the יבמה a גט, the brothers would share it equally instead. So the יבם promises a share up front. This promise is what רב יוסף will rule on next.

keyTerms.meaning: What is your thinking? What is your reason?

phrases.english: He said to him: What are you thinking?
phrases.notes: The brother who wants to do יבום is speaking to the brother who wanted to give the גט.

phrases.english: Is it because of the property?
I will split the property with you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the case begun in step 7 by giving the יבם's offer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יבם promises his brother half the property so the brother will not disqualify the יבמה with a גט.

steps.title: רב יוסף: a sale the רבנן forbade does not take effect
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that since the רבנן said not to sell, a sale made anyway is not a real sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Since the רבנן said he should not sell, even if he did sell, his sale is not a sale.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף decides the case. The promise to give away half the property is like a sale, and that kind of sale does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן told a יבם not to sell the property before he marries the יבמה. רב יוסף says this is more than advice. It cancels the deal itself. So the brother cannot collect the half he was promised.

keyTerms.meaning: His sale is a sale, meaning it is valid

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main argument of the section: does a sale the רבנן said not to make still take effect after the fact?

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Since the Rabbis said he should not sell,
even though he sold,
phrases.notes: Here the 'sale' is the promise to give his brother half the property.

phrases.english: his sale is not a sale.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: כֵּיוָן דַּאֲמוּר רַבָּנַן לָא לִיזַבֵּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling on the case told in steps 7 and 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the רבנן say not to sell, a sale made anyway does not take effect.

steps.title: The ברייתא that a יבם may not sell
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף supports himself with a ברייתא: even when the estate is far bigger than the כתובה, the יבם may not sell, because all the property is backing for her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: If a man died and left a woman waiting for יבום, and left property worth one hundred מנה, even though her כתובה is only one מנה, he may not sell, because all his property is guaranteed for her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a source showing that the רבנן did forbid a יבם to sell.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is extreme: the estate is worth a hundred times the כתובה, and still no selling is allowed. רב יוסף reads this as a real ban that cancels the sale, not just advice.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow waiting for her brother-in-law to do יבום or חליצה
A coin unit worth one hundred דינרים
Guaranteed, pledged as backing for a debt

steps.confusionAlert: Earlier, in steps 3 and 4, the line in the משנה about the כתובה was called advice. Here the ברייתא's 'he may not sell' is being read by רב יוסף as a real prohibition.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: מִי שֶׁמֵּת וְהִנִּיחַ שׁוֹמֶרֶת יָבָם,
phrases.english: As it was taught: One who died and left a widow waiting for her יבם,
and left property worth one hundred מנה,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכְּתוּבָּתָהּ אֵינָהּ אֶלָּא מָנֶה —
phrases.english: even though her כתובה is only one מנה,
he may not sell,
because all his property is guaranteed for her כתובה.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: מִי שֶׁמֵּת וְהִנִּיחַ שׁוֹמֶרֶת יָבָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יוסף's ruling in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that the רבנן forbade the יבם to sell
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: 'לֹא יִמְכּוֹר, שֶׁכׇּל נְכָסָיו אַחְרָאִין לִכְתוּבָּתָהּ'

steps.title: אביי: forbidden sales sometimes still hold
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks whether every 'don't sell' cancels the sale. A משנה shows that even when בית הלל say not to sell, everyone agrees the sale holds if it was done.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Is it true that wherever the רבנן said not to sell, if he sold anyway the sale is not a sale? But we learned: בית שמאי say she may sell, and בית הלל say she may not sell, and both agree that if she sold or gave it away, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף's general rule with a משנה that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that משנה, בית הלל say 'she may not sell.' Yet everyone agrees that a sale already made stands. So a ban on selling does not always cancel the sale, and רב יוסף's rule looks wrong.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל הֵיכָא דַּאֲמוּר רַבָּנַן לָא לִיזַבֵּין —
phrases.english: And anywhere the Rabbis said he should not sell,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּזַבֵּין לָא הֲוָה זְבִינֵיהּ זְבִינֵי?
phrases.english: even though he sold, his sale is not a sale?
But we learned: Beit Shammai say she may sell,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה about property a woman inherited while she was engaged (78a).

phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say she may not sell,
and both these and those agree
that if she sold or gave it away, it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְכׇל הֵיכָא דַּאֲמוּר רַבָּנַן לָא לִיזַבֵּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's rule from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's rule that a sale the רבנן forbade does not take effect
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the משנה, בית הלל forbid selling, yet everyone agrees a completed sale stands. So a ban on selling does not cancel the sale.

steps.title: רבי חנינא בר פפי sides with רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: The question is sent to רבי חנינא בר פפי, who replies that the הלכה follows רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent the question to רבי חנינא בר פפי. He sent back: like רב יוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: Since אביי and רב יוסף disagree, the case is sent to an outside authority, who rules for רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reply gives a ruling with no reasoning attached. It does not answer אביי's challenge from the משנה, and אביי will point to exactly that weakness next.

keyTerms.meaning: They sent it before him, meaning they sent him the question
Like רב יוסף: the halacha follows him

phrases.aramaic: שַׁלְחוּהָ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פַּפֵּי,
phrases.english: They sent it before Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi,
he sent back: Like Rav Yosef.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁלְחוּהָ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פַּפֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the dispute in steps 9 to 11 for now, in רב יוסף's favor.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The הלכה follows רב יוסף, given without a reason.

steps.title: אביי rejects a ruling with no reason
steps.stepSummary: אביי says רבי חנינא בר פפי's answer adds nothing, because he gave no reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Did רבי חנינא בר פפי hang jewelry on it?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on the ruling against him because it comes with no explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Hanging jewelry' means decorating something without adding anything real. A bare 'like רב יוסף' does not answer the משנה אביי quoted, so אביי says it carries no weight.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? Do you really think?
He hung jewelry on it: he only decorated it and added nothing real

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: אַטּוּ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פַּפֵּי כִּיפֵי תְּלָה לַהּ?
phrases.english: Did Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi hang jewelry on it?
phrases.notes: He means: just announcing 'like רב יוסף' with no reason doesn't actually prove anything.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אַטּוּ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פַּפֵּי כִּיפֵי תְּלָה לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the ruling given in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The authority of רבי חנינא בר פפי's ruling for רב יוסף
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It gives no reason and does not answer the challenge from the משנה.

steps.title: רב מניומי sides with אביי, open to more reasons
steps.stepSummary: The question is sent to רב מניומי בריה דרב נחומי, who rules like אביי, but asks to be told if רב יוסף has a different reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent it to רב מניומי the son of רב נחומי. He sent back: like אביי. And if רב יוסף gives a different reason for it, send it to me.
steps.whatsHappening: A second authority rules for אביי, so the promise to the brother does count. He stays willing to reconsider if רב יוסף has a better reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's reason, that a forbidden sale is void, is answered by אביי's משנה, so it falls. רב מניומי leaves the door open only if רב יוסף can bring a different reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Like אביי: the halacha follows him

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף: when the רבנן say 'don't sell,' a sale made anyway is void. אביי: a forbidden sale can still take effect, as in the משנה where everyone agrees it stands. The final ruling sent back follows אביי, unless רב יוסף gives a new reason.

phrases.aramaic: שַׁלְחוּהָ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב מִנְיוֹמֵי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נְחוּמִי,
phrases.english: They sent it before Rav Minyumi, son of Rav Nechumi,
he sent back: Like Abaye,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמַר בַּהּ רַב יוֹסֵף טַעְמָא אַחֲרִינָא שִׁלְחוּ לִי.
phrases.english: and if Rav Yosef says a different reason for it, send it to me.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁלְחוּהָ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב מִנְיוֹמֵי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נְחוּמִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אביי rejects the first ruling in step 13, a second authority rules for אביי.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows אביי: a sale the רבנן said not to make can still take effect, so the יבם's promise counts, unless רב יוסף brings a different reason.

steps.title: רב יוסף finds a ברייתא about a debt owed to the dead brother
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף brings a ברייתא: a יבם who owed his dead brother money cannot keep it. It is taken from him to buy land for the כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף went, searched carefully, and found a ברייתא. It says: if a man was owed money by his brother, then died and left a widow waiting for יבום, the brother cannot say, 'Since I inherit, the money is now mine.' Instead, the money is taken from the יבם, land is bought with it, and he eats the produce.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a new source to prove that a יבם cannot freely use his dead brother's property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The money the יבם owed is part of the dead brother's estate, so it is backing for the widow's כתובה. If even this debt is taken from him and turned into land, then he certainly may not sell the estate. The יבם keeps only the right to eat the produce of that land.

keyTerms.meaning: a creditor, someone who is owed money
a widow waiting for her יבם to marry her or do חליצה
eats the produce, uses the yield but not the land itself

phrases.english: Rav Yosef went out, examined carefully, and found
that it is taught in a ברייתא:
If a man was owed money by his brother,
and he died and left a widow waiting for יבום,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יֹאמַר: הוֹאִיל וְשֶׁאֲנִי יוֹרֵשׁ — הֶחְזַקְתִּי,
phrases.english: he may not say: 'Since I inherit, I have taken possession,'
phrases.notes: The speaker is the brother who borrowed the money. He is now the יבם.

phrases.english: rather, they take the money out of the יבם's hands,
and land is bought with it,
and he eats the produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְפַק רַב יוֹסֵף דָּק וְאַשְׁכַּח דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אביי's view was accepted, רב יוסף looks for new support for his own position.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's ruling that a יבם may not sell or take for himself the dead brother's property
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that forces the debt out of the יבם's hands to buy land for the כתובה

steps.title: אביי: maybe it is just good advice
steps.stepSummary: אביי suggests the ברייתא only gives the יבם helpful advice. It is not a binding rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Maybe they did for him what is good for him.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's proof by reading the ברייתא as friendly advice instead of a strict law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If buying land is only a smart suggestion that protects the money, then the ברייתא does not prove the יבם is forbidden to use it. Without a requirement, there is no proof that a sale would be cancelled.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Perhaps they did for him what is good for him.
phrases.notes: He means the land purchase is advice that helps the יבם. It is not something forced on him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the ברייתא brought in step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא, not the ברייתא itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may be advice rather than a binding requirement.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the word 'they take out' means it is forced
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that מוציאין means taking against his will, so this cannot be mere advice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: The ברייתא says 'they take it out,' and you say they did what is good for him?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends his proof by pointing to the exact wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You do not 'take money out' of someone's hands just to give him advice. The word מוציאין shows force, so the ברייתא is a binding rule, and רב יוסף's proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: the teacher of the ברייתא teaches

phrases.english: He said to him:
The teacher of the ברייתא says 'they take it out,'

phrases.aramaic: וְאַתְּ אָמְרַתְּ דְּטָבָא לֵיהּ עֲבַדוּ לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: and you say they did for him what is good for him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's rejection in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the ברייתא's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא could be read as helpful advice.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word מוציאין shows the money is taken by force, so it is a binding law.

steps.title: רב נחמן: this ברייתא is not reliable
steps.stepSummary: The question goes back to רב מניומי, who quotes רב נחמן: this ברייתא is not a reliable source.
steps.simpleTranslation: They again sent the question before רב מניומי son of רב נחומי. He told them: This is what רב יוסף בר מניומי said in the name of רב נחמן: This is not a משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב יוסף's proof seemed to work, the question is sent to a scholar, and he knocks out the source itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's reading of the wording may be correct, but the ברייתא is declared not authoritative. So it cannot serve as proof. This attacks the source itself, not how it was read.

keyTerms.meaning: this is not a reliable teaching, so we do not rely on it

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'משנה' does not mean the book of משנה. It means this ברייתא is not a trustworthy teaching to rely on.

phrases.english: They again sent it before
Rav Minyumi, son of Rav Nechumi.
He said to them: So said

phrases.aramaic: רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef bar Minyumi, that Rav Nachman said:
This is not a reliable teaching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overrides רב יוסף's defense by rejecting the ברייתא altogether.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The entire ברייתא as a source
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא is not authoritative, so no proof can come from it.

steps.title: Why is the ברייתא rejected? A first suggestion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא is rejected. It suggests it is because a debt counts as movable property, which does not back a כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? If you say it is because the money counts as movable property, and movable property does not back a כתובה...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב נחמן's rejection and offers a first guess, which it will test in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion is that a debt is only movable property, not land. By the usual rule, movable property is not backing for a כתובה. If so, why would the ברייתא say the debt must go to the כתובה?

keyTerms.meaning: if you say, a suggested answer that may be rejected
are pledged as backing for a debt

phrases.english: What is the reason?
If you say it is because they count as movable property,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the money the יבם owed, which is not land.

phrases.english: and movable property is not pledged for a כתובה —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the rejection in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the ברייתא is considered unreliable

steps.title: That reason fails: the ברייתא may follow רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the first suggestion. The ברייתא could follow רבי מאיר, who holds that movable property does back a כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it follows רבי מאיר, who said that movable property is pledged for a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the first suggested reason for rejecting the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא is not thrown out just because it follows a minority view. Since רבי מאיר holds that movable property backs a כתובה, the ברייתא fits his view. So this cannot be why רב נחמן rejected it.

phrases.english: Perhaps it follows Rabbi Meir,
who said: movable property is pledged for a כתובה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reason suggested in step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the suggested reason, not רב נחמן's ruling
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא could follow רבי מאיר, so movable property is not a reason to reject it.

steps.title: The real reason: she is not his litigant
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב נחמן rejected the ברייתא because the debtor can tell the יבמה, 'You are not my litigant.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the reason is that he can say to her: You are not someone I have a case with.
steps.whatsHappening: The first explanation for rejecting the ברייתא did not work, so the גמרא offers a new one. The person who owes the money can tell the woman that his business was with her husband, not with her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 20 the גמרא showed that the 'movable property' reason fails, because the ברייתא could follow רבי מאיר. So it needs a different flaw. The new flaw is about who has the right to sue: the debtor owed the money to the dead brother, so the יבמה has no direct claim against him. That is why the ברייתא cannot be relied on.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; introduces a new answer after the first one was rejected
A litigant; the other party in a legal case

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא is not rejected because a debt is movable property. It is rejected because the debtor never had any dealings with the יבמה, so she cannot sue him directly.
steps.confusionAlert: The claim 'you are not my litigant' is only about who may sue. He is saying his debt was with her husband, so she has no direct claim against him.

phrases.english: Rather, it is because he can say to her:
phrases.notes: 'He' is the man who owed money to the dead brother; 'her' is the יבמה trying to collect for her כתובה.

phrases.aramaic: אַתְּ לָאו בַּעֲלַת דְּבָרִים דִּידִי אַתְּ.
phrases.english: You are not my litigant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation from Step 19, which Step 20 rejected, with a new reason for רב נחמן's rejection of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason replacing a rejected explanation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was thought to be rejected because a debt is movable property, which does not back a כתובה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is rejected because the debtor can claim that the יבמה is not his litigant, since his debt was owed to the dead brother.
